ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
You can make only one rectangle with the perimeter consisting of 6 matches (see the picture). How many different rectangles with the perimeter consisting of 14 matches can you compose?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is a rectangular outline made of matches. The upper side is made of 2 horizontal matches, and the lower side is also made of 2 horizontal matches; the left side and the right side are each made of 1 vertical match. So the number of perimeter matches of this example rectangle is 2+2+1+1=6. Then reason: This indicates that the side lengths of the rectangle are counted by whole matches, and the same size after rotation is not counted as a different rectangle. Suppose the two adjacent side lengths of a rectangle made of 14 matches are positive integers a and b respectively, then the perimeter is 2a+2b=14, so a+b=7. The unordered combinations of positive integers are (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), a total of 3 types. Therefore the answer is 3.
